title: I Took the Zoo Member Early-Entry Scan to the Guest Who Tailgated

parts.text: I scanned at 8:01 a.m. for member early entry and a guest slid under my arm. The gate sign the guest relations lead posted said: ONE SCAN, ONE BODY. GUESTS AFTER 9. I was thirty-nine, member since 2019, holding a coffee and a camera for the panda cam. Guest relations pal Rio said, "They're with education." The guest wore a birthday pin. I photographed the pin, the sign, and the unmatched scan. Then I took the still to membership services. At 8:07 membership asked why a birthday pin was on an early-entry tailgate ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Membership can see a birthday pin under my scan against the one-body sign.

social.video_title: A birthday pin tailgated member early entry — Part 1/2
social.description: 8:01 scan, a slide under my arm, and a one-body sign. I walked it to membership. Would you have blocked the gate?

parts.text: Rio called it a courtesy until the turnstile log showed one scan two bodies. I printed the ticket, the sign, and the photo. The guest waited at the plaza until 9. Rio told education the sign was always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when a pin is in a still. Gate policy now has a second line: EDUCATION IS NOT A SLIDE. I see pandas at 8. Birthday waits. The turnstile finally counts bodies.

social.video_title: Education is not a gate slide — Part 2/2
social.description: Tailgate ticket, a plaza wait until 9, and a second line on the sign. Was courtesy ever two bodies?
